newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Telstra sees future price cuts.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Telstra sees future price cuts.

text.p: The Australian government's Telstra Corp Ltd said on Friday it expected further price reductions and the introduction of open competition in 1997 would create formidable challenges.

"It is critical that the Corporation continues to make efficiency gains and, indeed, accelerates these gains, if we are to compete effectively with our global and domestic competitors," Telstra chief executive Frank Blount said.
Earlier, Telstra posted a 31.5 percent rise in net profit for 1995/96 of A$2.30 billion.

"With open competition being introduced in 1997, further price reductions, and the consequences of industry convergence, globalisation and technological changes, the challenges facing Telstra remain formidable," Blount said.

"Without productivity improvements, Telstra will not be able to deliver price decreases, service levels, employment standards and increased investments and dividends that its stakeholders demand," he said.
Telstra said earlier it planned a A$1.1 billion provision in its 1996/97 accounts to reflect expected redundancies.
Telstra said in July it planned to cut its current staff of about 74,000 workers by 9,000 in the 1996/97 year.
It said later on Friday it planned to cut numbers by 6,000 in 1997/98 and a further 7,000 in 1998/99.
